caseNidaan.title: NidaanPartner.com — a multi-office claims operation running on software we built end to end
caseNidaan.lede: Nidaan – The Legal Consultants LLP recovers insurance claims that insurers rejected, underpaid or stalled. Running that across multiple offices, a panel of physicians, advocates and surveyors, and a network of insurance advisors is not a website problem — it is an operations-control problem. GoLuQ built the entire control layer.
caseNidaan.role: GoLuQ's Principal Architect is Co-Founder & Tech Architect at Nidaan — this system was designed from inside the operation, not specified from outside it.
caseNidaan.statsTitle: What the operation runs at today
caseNidaan.statsNote: Operational figures as published by Nidaan – The Legal Consultants LLP.
caseNidaan.buildLede: The heart of the build: one control plane that lets head office run every branch, and every branch run its own desk — without the two ever colliding.

modules.d: Head office, regional offices and branch desks modelled as a real hierarchy. Every case, document and payment belongs to a branch and rolls up automatically.
Claim experts, panel physicians, senior advocates and licensed surveyors each see exactly their own queue — and nothing from another branch's caseload.
Intake → medical review → TPA challenge → Competent Authority or Consumer Court filing → settlement. Every stage owned, dated and auditable.
Insurance advisors file and track multi-claim submissions from their own dashboard, mapped to their own branch, with white-labelled client reporting.
Silver, Gold and Platinum tiers with per-plan claim quotas and sum-insured caps enforced by the system — not by a spreadsheet and a phone call.
Head office sees performance by branch, by advisor and by claim type in one view. Each branch sees only its own. Same data, different altitude.

caseNidaan.scaleTitle: Built so the next branch is a configuration entry, not a rebuild
caseNidaan.scaleBody: Nidaan's desks today run across Indore and Bhopal, serving policyholders in Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Punjab. The control layer was never designed for four offices — it was designed so that the fortieth office is a configuration entry. Create the branch, assign the roles, and its cases, advisors, quotas and reporting exist from that moment.

process.title: Five steps, with dates attached
process.lede: Scope ambiguity is what makes custom software frightening. Here is exactly what happens and when.

steps.d: You describe how the work moves through your firm today. We map it and tell you honestly whether a custom build is the right call — including when it isn't.
A written architecture: screens, data model, integrations, infrastructure plan, and a fixed-scope price. Yours to keep even if you stop here.
Working demos every week on your own staging URL. You watch it take shape, and changes cost the least at this stage.
Deployed to your cloud account. Source code in your Git organisation, IP transfer signed. Your team trained in Hindi or English until they run it without us.
Take a support retainer, or take nothing at all. Your system, your infrastructure, your call — and that stays true forever.

items.a: Your code lives in your Git organisation and your system runs in your cloud account — both from delivery day, not as a parting gift. You get architecture documentation, a dependency inventory and an access map. Any competent engineering team can pick it up cold. This is the single biggest risk in custom software, and the structure above is how it gets removed.

items.q: Who maintains it in year three?
items.a: Your choice. A support retainer with us, your own hired engineer, or another firm entirely — the code is yours and it is documented for exactly that. If you take nothing, the system keeps running; you simply take on patching yourself.

That is assumed, not an exception. Training in plain Hindi or English is included, and we stay until your team runs it comfortably on their own. The systems we build get used by front-desk staff and branch clerks every day.

Often, yes — and when it is, we will tell you on the call rather than take the project. Custom wins when the workflow is genuinely specific to you, or when per-seat pricing compounds against your headcount. Below that line, buy the product.

items.q: How do I know the estimate holds?
items.a: The blueprint stage produces a fixed-scope price before any build work starts. Scope changes are quoted separately and approved by you in writing before they are built. You never receive a surprise invoice.

items.q: How long before we're actually using it?
items.a: A focused first version typically reaches your team in 8–12 weeks. We deliberately scope a working first release rather than a complete one — you start getting value while the rest is built.

tco.honestTitle: When SaaS is the right decision
tco.honestBody: Under roughly fifteen seats on a genuinely commodity workflow, buy the product. It will be faster to deploy and cheaper across the horizon, and we will tell you so in the session rather than take the engagement. Custom becomes correct when the workflow is a genuine differentiator, when per-seat cost compounds against headcount, or when data sovereignty is a regulatory requirement rather than a preference.

verticals.complianceBody: GoLuQ does not hold HIPAA, SOC 2, ISO 27001, GDPR or ADHICS certification, and will never claim to. What we provide is engineering: encryption in transit and at rest, least-privilege access models, immutable audit logging, and single-tenant isolation — built so that the certification you hold, on the infrastructure you control, withstands your audit. Certification attaches to your organisation and your environment. We build to survive the assessment; we do not sell you a badge.

process.title: Five phases, with the IP transfer point marked
process.lede: Scope ambiguity is the real risk in custom engineering. Here is precisely how an engagement runs.

steps.d: You describe the operation. We return an architectural opinion — including a direct recommendation against building, when that's the honest answer.
Written architecture: data model, service boundaries, integration surface, infrastructure and security design, and a fixed-scope price. Yours regardless of what you do next.
Weekly working increments on your staging environment. Change is cheapest here, and it's designed to be seen early.
Deployed to your cloud account. Source in your Git organisation. IP transfer agreement executed. Architecture documentation, dependency inventory and access model delivered.
Support retainer, engineering blocks, or nothing at all. The system is yours and it keeps running either way.

items.q: Key-person risk — what if you become unavailable?
items.a: Your source lives in your Git organisation and the system runs in your cloud account from delivery, not as a contingency. You receive architecture documentation, a full dependency inventory and a documented access model. Any competent engineering team continues from a cold start. This is the central risk in boutique engagement, and the structure is designed specifically to remove it.

items.q: Who maintains this in year three?
items.a: Your decision: a retainer with us, your own team, or another firm. The code is yours and documented for exactly that scenario. With no retainer the system continues to run; you assume patching and dependency upkeep.

items.q: Will this pass our security review?
items.a: You receive architecture documentation, a dependency inventory with licence audit, the access and authorisation model, audit-log design, and the infrastructure-as-code that provisions the environment. It runs in your tenancy under your existing controls, which is usually the shortest path through an assessment, not the longest.

items.q: How do you handle delivery across time zones?
items.a: The Principal Architect has delivered across APAC, EMEA, North America and the Gulf for twenty years, including at DXC, Cornerstone OnDemand and HighLevel. Fixed weekly overlap hours are agreed at contract, all decisions are written, and every increment is inspectable on your own staging environment rather than described to you on a call.

items.q: Where does our data sit, and who can reach it?
items.a: In your cloud account, in the region you select, under access keys you hold. Engineering access is scoped, time-boxed and logged, and is revoked entirely at handover. There is no GoLuQ-controlled copy of your production data.

The blueprint fixes scope and price before build begins. Changes are quoted separately and approved in writing before implementation. There are no surprise invoices, and no discovery of scope halfway through.
